newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka paper hails Mahathir as Asia's leader.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka paper hails Mahathir as Asia's leader.

text.p: Sri Lanka's government-run Daily News hailed Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad as Asia's new leader on Saturday after his outspoken rejection of Western interference in the region's affairs.
The newspaper, which tends to reflect closely the opinion of the Sri Lankan government, said Mahathir was a "Godsend" for the Third World and Asia.

"Here's one Asian leader who doesn't see Red on confronting a white skin. Nor is he overawed by the military and economic might of the West. As far as Asia is concerned, Mahathir, indeed, seems to be the long awaited model leader," the Daily News said in an editorial.
In an address to foreign ministers of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) on Thursday, the Malaysian leader said outsiders should keep out of the region's business.
"We will resolve our problems in our own way and in our own time. No one, but no one, should assume that only they know the solutions to all problems," he said.

Mahathir has made a series of attacks on financial speculators in recent days, accusing them of deliberately undermining Southeast Asian currencies and calling them "robbers", "anarchists" and "brigands".
On Saturday, Mahathir named U.S. based financier George Soros as the man responsible for the current decline in the Malaysian ringgit, the Malaysian news agency Bernama reported.
The Daily news praised what it said was a new sense of independence in the region.

"There seems to be a flowering in Southeast Asia, for instance, a sturdy independence of spirit, an attitudinal change which sees through Western designs and the demeaning ideological baggage the West has been heaping on the East to keep it in servitude," it said.
Most Asian countries were bound to marvel at Mahathir's daring, it said.

"Whether it be in human rights or the restructuring of the U.N., to better represent a changed global power balance, Mahathir has proved to be a Godsend for the Third World in general and the Asiatic region in particular.
"On all these hotly debated issues, the Malaysian leader has almost single-handed taken on the West and fearlessly championed the views of the less advantaged sections of the world community.
"He has told the West 'where to get off'," it said.
